Devices
de-VY-sez
noun (plural)
From the Old French devis, a division or arrangement, and that from the Latin dividere, to divide — hence a thing devised, a plan, contrivance, or scheme. A device is thought worked into a design.

Biblical Definition

A device in Scripture is a contrivance of the mind, and the word is used of three schemers. Men devise: “There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand” (Pro 19:21) — the two halves of that verse hold the whole doctrine of providence, human plans genuinely made and a divine counsel that is not thereby put at risk. The wicked devise in particular: “The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined” (Psa 10:2), a prayer that the trap should catch the trapper, which is the regular shape of biblical justice — Haman on his own gallows. Satan devises: “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices” (2Co 2:11) — and the context of that famous sentence is worth recovering, for Paul is not warning about the occult or gross temptation but about a church failing to forgive a repentant offender. That is the devil’s device in view: a congregation so severe with a restored sinner that he is swallowed up with overmuch sorrow. And God overrules all devising: “He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise” (Job 5:12). Three devisers, and only one counsel that stands.

Webster 1828 Definition

Contrivances, schemes, or plans formed in the mind; used of the plans of men, the plots of the wicked, and the stratagems of Satan.

DEVICE, n. That which is formed by design; a contrivance; an invention.

A scheme formed; a project; stratagem; artifice; often in an ill sense.

An emblem or figure designed to represent a family or a purpose.

From the Old French devis; Latin dividere, to divide, to distribute.

2Co 2:11: we are not ignorant of his devices — the stratagems of Satan.

Key Scripture

Job 5:12 — "He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise."

Psa 10:2 — "The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor: let them be taken in the devices that they have imagined."

Pro 19:21 — "There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand."

2Co 2:11 — "Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices."

Modern Corruption

2Co 2:11 is quoted almost exclusively in warnings about the occult or gross temptation, when Paul’s stated context is a church refusing to restore a repentant man.

expand to see more

The corruption is the misdirection of a famous verse. We are not ignorant of his devices has become the standard epigraph for teaching on spiritual warfare in its dramatic forms — the occult, the demonic, the sensational temptation — and while Satan certainly works in those ways, that is not what Paul is discussing. Read the preceding verses. A man had been disciplined by the Corinthian church; the punishment inflicted of many was sufficient; and Paul urges them to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow. Then: lest Satan get an advantage of us, for we are not ignorant of his devices. The device is unforgiveness in a congregation that was right to discipline and is now wrong to withhold restoration.

Recover the plain sense: the adversary works most successfully through churches doing something legitimate slightly too long. Discipline is commanded; discipline that will not end when repentance comes is a trap, and Paul says plainly whose trap it is. That is a searching thought for congregations proud of their seriousness. Set it beside Pro 19:21 for the comfort that governs the whole subject: men devise and the devil devises, and the counsel of the LORD shall stand. Job 5:12 completes it — God disappoints the devices of the crafty so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise. The schemes are real; not one of them is sovereign.
